newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico not considering Brady buyback in short-term.
newsitem.headline: Mexico not considering Brady buyback in short-term.

text.p: Mexico is not considering another buyback of its outstanding Brady bonds in the short-term, Deputy Finance Minister Martin Werner told analysts in a conference call on Wednesday.

In response to a question on whether Mexico could retire some more Brady bonds, Werner said, "In the short-term, we are not looking at that, but in the medium-term we still think that collateralized debt is inefficient and that there are gains both to Mexico and to the market to take out that debt."
In May last year, Mexico placed a 30-year bond and bought back outstanding par and discount Brady bonds with a market value worth about $1.75 billion.
Mexico placed a 20-year bond in later in the year and used those proceeds along with other funds to buy back outstanding Brady bonds worth about $1.24 billion.
There have been market rumours that Mexico would buy back its outstanding Aztec Brady bonds shortly.
Werner also said that Mexico will continue to look at placing debt in other currencies than in U.S. dollars.

"We will be continuing to look at different markets to extend the maturities of our debt and also given that we are issuing significant amounts in non-dollar currencies, we will focus on managing the currency exposure that we are taking by issuing non-dollar debt," Werner said.
Mexico is rumoured to be ready to issue a 50 billion yen bond with a seven-year maturity.
That issue could come as early as this week, sources in Tokyo told Reuters.
